understand.concept: Character classes and special sequences describe which characters may appear at a position. Quantifiers control how many repetitions are allowed. For example, [A-Z] matches one uppercase ASCII letter, \d matches a Unicode decimal digit by default, and {3} requires exactly three repetitions.
understand.whyItMatters: These building blocks let a pattern express compact formats such as codes, identifiers and separated values.
understand.analogy: Character classes define which symbols may enter a slot, while quantifiers specify how many slots are required.
understand.analogyLimit: Character classes and quantifiers do not automatically enforce an entire field's format; anchors or fullmatch are needed when the whole string must conform.
understand.summary: Regex Character Classes, Special Sequences and Quantifiers teaches readable and predictable pattern matching with Python's re module.

explain.narrative:
## Character classes and repetition
Square brackets define a set or range, such as `[aeiou]` or `[A-Z]`. Special sequences include `\d` (digit), `\w` (word character) and `\s` (whitespace); their Unicode behaviour can matter for international text. A dot matches most characters except newline unless DOTALL is enabled.

Quantifiers include `*` for zero or more, `+` for one or more, `?` for zero or one, and `{m,n}` for a bounded count. Quantifiers are greedy by default. Use specific patterns and bounded repetition where possible.

examples.explanation: The character class matches any one of the listed vowels.

examples.title: Find digit sequences
examples.explanation: \d matches a digit and + groups one or more consecutive digits.

examples.title: Match word and whitespace groups
examples.code:
import re
print(re.findall(r'\w+', 'red blue_2'))
print(re.findall(r'\s+', 'red   blue'))
examples.explanation: \w matches word characters and \s matches whitespace.

examples.title: Use exact and bounded repetition
examples.explanation: {4} requires exactly four digits; {2,4} allows two through four.

examples.title: Distinguish optional and required characters
examples.code:
import re
pattern = r'colou?r'
print(bool(re.fullmatch(pattern, 'color')))
print(bool(re.fullmatch(pattern, 'colour')))
examples.explanation: The question mark allows the preceding u to appear zero or one time.

practise.independentTask: Extract words, digit groups and whitespace runs from a sample sentence. Explain how each special sequence and quantifier affects the result.
hints: Use square brackets for one character from a set.
Use \d, \w and \s for common character categories.
Use + for one or more and * for zero or more.
Use {n} for an exact count and {m,n} for a range.
Use fullmatch when the complete input must follow the pattern.
